title: Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (VI: Liver King, Alex Eubank, Jujimufu...)
summary: Part 6 of NH's series grading fitness YouTubers on 20 criteria scored 0-10 (200 max). Basement Bodybuilding scores 136.5, Peter Katcherian 134, Jujimufu 131, Liver King 103 and Alex Eubank 93. His recurring standards: training value over entertainment, honesty about drug status, no supplement selling, and not blackpilling natural lifters.
claims: His grading system scores 20 criteria from 0 to 10 for 200 points, and he grades harshly, so 130 is not a bad score

Peter Katcherian's programming is old-school Golden Era advice that is time-tested and works for naturals; his 27 dollar program is good, apart from some leg-training gaps and too much shoulder emphasis
He prefers experience-based 'bro science' grounded in logic over purely evidence-based coaching, though it narrows your horizons
Golden Era methods can blackpill naturals: if the coach preaching them is enhanced, as all the Golden Era stars were, natural followers get no Dorian-like results and may quit

He suspects Katcherian is enhanced because of back acne across his shoulders and upper back and a 'TRT daddy' look; claiming 5 ft 10 and 190 lb while looking bigger than NH at 6 ft and 210 lb does not add up
Katcherian scores 10 on supplements: he could make a fortune selling 'Golden Era' supplements but does not
Jujimufu used to make thoughtful whiteboard programming videos but now produces circus entertainment where you watch other people train and learn little
Jujimufu's transformation is blackpilling: he got bigger by upping the dose, not through his training methods
Smelling salts are a meme; if you need them to lift, rethink your approach because it is not sustainable
Nearly every channel with a million subscribers clickbaits, because without it you get 50k views and the channel dies
Alex Eubank teaches almost no programming (his Greek God program is poor), and staying permanently lean while trying to grow sends young men a terrible message
Taking on 7-8 sponsors right after blowing up shows low integrity: selling merchandise that does nothing for muscle
Aesthetic influencers who hang out with enhanced lifters and keep teasing their own natty status blackpill young viewers
Pre-fatiguing the quads before squats is a bro-science meme, though not dangerous
Supplement powders do not build muscle; only training and food do
Aesthetic influencers look bigger than they are through lighting, pump and camera tricks; Eubank is about 170 lb but looks bigger than NH
Basement Bodybuilding scores 8.5 on programming: content focused on hypertrophy methodology that always shows how to apply it to your own training
Fighting powerlifting dogma for hypertrophy is good, but it risks building a new hypertrophy-only dogma that will not serve lifters who care about strength
Never mentioning drugs at all, as Basement Bodybuilding does, is the least blackpilling approach, though it leaves out viewers already influenced by PED preachers
Good science-based coaching is a mix of bro scientist and real scientist, which is almost impossible to achieve
Fitness topics are finite, so channels eventually run out of new things to say unless they recycle or get creative
Liver King's training (more time walking than lifting, overhead pressing a roughly 40 lb tree branch, walking with a 10 lb chain) looks impressive but builds nothing without drugs
Liver King gets zero integrity not for using drugs but for lying; an honest drug user selling products would be acceptable
Liver King's ancestral tenets, like sunlight, walking and social connection, are not dumb in themselves; the problem was the marketing
Polarizing all-or-nothing personalities attract more followers than nuanced ones
Cooking meat is sensible: it eases digestion, saves energy and kills parasites
Selling organ meat supplements works because people find real organ meat smelly, unappetizing and hard to source, so the pill becomes the easy path
Liver King has a 'spider physique' (bloated belly, small limbs) despite heavy drug use; at 5 ft 7 he probably weighs less than the 200 lb he claims, so drugs alone do not make a physique
He has a job, is married and owns a house
